name: PRIME

paper.title: PRIME: Large Language Model Personalization with Cognitive Dual-Memory and Personalized Thought Process

construction.unit: per-user LoRA adapter (semantic memory); raw past threads (episodic memory, variants only)
construction.kept_as: parametric: the user's history is trained into LoRA weights; episodic threads stored verbatim
construction.processing: LoRA task fine-tuning on the user's past CMV threads (query -> delta-awarded reply), then self-distilled personalized thinking (profile, replay, rejection sampling, proxy-written thoughts, 1-epoch fine-tune)
construction.writer: LoRA training of the base model (Llama, Qwen, Ministral or Phi, 3B-14B)

organization.structure: one LoRA adapter per user (+ raw thread list in EM variants)
organization.stores: semantic memory: LoRA weights ΔH(a); episodic memory: past engagements (dropped in final PRIME)

management.operations: none after instantiation: both memories are frozen

retrieval.query: the new query (OP and candidate replies)
retrieval.candidates: final PRIME: none, the user's LoRA is merged into the model; EM variants: 3 most recent threads (CMV) or 4 (LaMP)
retrieval.selection: recency in EM variants; relevance retrieval tested in §4 (retriever not named)

use.context: the query only; the model with the user's LoRA writes a thinking trace that restates the user profile before answering
use.reasoning: one generation of up to 2,048 tokens: user experience, OP summary, outline, per-candidate analysis, reflection, answer

classify.note: Final PRIME keeps each user's history only as LoRA weights: no stored text is searched, and the memory is trained once and frozen (placed under append-only as the nearest value: nothing is edited or deleted). The episodic store of raw threads exists only in the EM, DUAL and EM-included variants.

stages.ingestion: A user's history is their past engagements: for CMV, single-turn Reddit threads (OP plus direct replies, one marked by the OP's delta); for LaMP, the benchmark's user profiles.
stages.construction: Semantic memory: a LoRA adapter per user trained with task-oriented fine-tuning (query with candidates -> the delta-awarded reply's option ID) for 3 epochs (2 on LaMP). Episodic memory: the raw engagements, stored as is.
stages.retrieval: At test time the user's LoRA is merged into the base model. EM variants also prepend the 3 (CMV) or 4 (LaMP) most recent engagements; the final PRIME drops this because it lowered scores.
stages.answer: The model generates a personalized thinking trace (user-experience summary, OP summary, outline, analysis of each candidate, reflection) and then the ranked top-3 option IDs, up to 2,048 tokens.
stages.learning: Personalized thinking is self-distilled: the LoRA model writes a user profile, replays the user's past threads as queries and keeps those it gets right; a proxy model (base model + profile text) writes structured thoughts given query and gold answer; thoughts reaching the gold answer are kept and the LoRA model is fine-tuned on them for one epoch.

summary: Cognitive dual-memory framing of LLM personalization: episodic memory as recalled past engagements and semantic memory as a per-user LoRA, plus self-distilled personalized thinking; the final system keeps only the LoRA and the thinking, evaluated on a new Reddit ChangeMyView ranking dataset and LaMP.
notes: Venue verified on ACL Anthology: EMNLP 2025 main, pages 33707-33736 (2025.emnlp-main.1711). PDF read: arXiv v3 (26 Sep 2025). The linked repository (launchnlp/LM_Personalization, HEAD 14e4adbd80b75148bcb23e3080256e5b769a7e8b, 2025-06-25) contains only the CMV data and a README saying the code is still being refactored, so nothing here comes from code. New benchmark ids proposed in .cache/annot/new_benchmarks_prime.json ('cmv-persuasion', 'lamp'); new baselines in .cache/annot/new_extra_prime.json ('r1-distill', 'oppu'). Final PRIME excludes episodic memory (§6 Implementation Details, Table A3), so 'dual memory' applies to the DUAL and EM-included PRIME variants. The paper uses 'episodic memory' in two ways: recalled raw engagements (§4) and, in the profile-replacement study, the textual profile summary (App. D). Footnote 18 gives the Qwen2.5-14B model card as Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, apparently a typo.

sources.paper: arXiv 2507.04607v3 (PDF read 2026-09-30); ACL Anthology 2025.emnlp-main.1711 checked for venue
sources.code_note: The paper links https://github.com/launchnlp/LM_Personalization; at commit 14e4adbd80b75148bcb23e3080256e5b769a7e8b (latest, 2025-06-25) it holds only the CMV dataset (history, evaluation, target authors) and states that the code is still being refactored. No method code, so everything below is from the paper.

abstract.text: PRIME frames LLM personalization with the cognitive split between episodic memory (specific past engagements of a user) and semantic memory (lasting beliefs and preferences). The authors first compare many ways to build each memory, finding that recency beats relevance for recall and that per-user LoRA fine-tuning on the task is the strongest semantic memory. PRIME combines these and adds personalized thinking, learned by self-distilling reasoning traces from the user's own history. They also release a Reddit ChangeMyView dataset where the model must rank the reply that changed a user's view, and report gains over non-personalized and generic-reasoning baselines on it and on LaMP.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

headline: In the final PRIME a user's history lives only in a per-user LoRA adapter; no stored text is retrieved at test time.
The episodic part (recent past threads in the prompt) was dropped from the final system because it lowered scores; the dual memory survives only in the DUAL and EM-included variants.
The model restates a user profile at the start of its own thinking, a behaviour learned by self-distillation on the user's past threads.

units.name: Semantic memory
units.role: the user's preferences and beliefs, trained into weights
units.made_by: LoRA task fine-tuning on the user's history, then fine-tuning on self-distilled thoughts

fields.name: LoRA weights ΔH(a)
fields.what: one adapter per user, merged into the base model at test time (θ + ΔH(a))

fields.name: profile summary
fields.what: text summary of the user written by the LoRA model (Parametric Knowledge Reification); used to build the proxy model for thought synthesis, and regenerated by PRIME inside its thinking

units.name: Episodic memory
units.role: specific past engagements of the user
units.made_by: none: raw threads stored as is

fields.name: past threads
fields.what: the user's single-turn CMV threads (OP and replies) or LaMP profile items; 3 (CMV) or 4 (LaMP) most recent are prepended in EM and DUAL variants; not used by final PRIME

write.how: task-oriented fine-tuning per user: input is a past OP with candidate replies, target is the delta-awarded reply's option ID
the LoRA model summarises the user (PKR)
each past engagement is turned into a query; keep those the LoRA model answers correctly
a proxy model (base model + profile text) is given the query and its answer and writes structured thoughts that restate the profile; keep those whose answer matches
train the LoRA model 1 epoch with cross-entropy: plain query in, thinking trace + answer out

read.how: merge the user's LoRA into the base model
prepend the 3 most recent engagements (CMV) before the new OP; not in final PRIME
one generation: user experience, OP summary, outline, per-candidate analysis, reflection, ranked answer

answer_context.sees: the query only (author name, OP title and body, candidate replies as JSON); personalization comes from the merged LoRA weights
answer_context.format: standard CMV template (Fig. A7) followed by the personalized-thinking output instructions (Fig. A10)

compression.what: user history vs what the answer model reads
compression.basis: Not comparable in tokens: final PRIME reads no history text; the history (183.2 engagements per CMV user on average, Table A1) is held in LoRA weights whose rank and size are not reported.

open_questions: The LoRA rank, learning rate and adapter size are not reported, so the memory capacity per user is unknown.
PRIME vs SM mixes two changes (thought fine-tuning and a longer generation with a structured prompt); a SM + thinking-prompt-without-training variant is not reported for the trained models.
Only 133 CMV queries from 41 users; results average 10 runs but no variance is given.

The adapter then learns to think in a personalized way from its own filtered answers and proxy-written thoughts, fine-tuned for one epoch.

components.model: per-user LoRA on the base model (Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Ministral-8B, Qwen2.5-7B/14B, Phi-4; instruct versions)
proxy: same base model + textual profile

ablation.src: paper Table A3 (CMV, Avg of Hit@1, Hit@3, DCG@3, MRR; 10 runs)

discussion.takeaway: For personalization, a per-user LoRA trained on the task beats recalling past engagements, and teaching that adapter to reason from a recalled profile adds more; the recalled engagements themselves were left out of the final system.

claims.evidence: SM vs EM Avg on CMV: 31.24 vs 26.88 (Llama-3.1-8B), 37.22 vs 30.65 (Qwen2.5-14B); same trend on LaMP (Tables 3-4, A3).

claims.claim: Recency recall beats relevance retrieval for episodic memory.
Personalized thinking is crucial and PRIME is model-agnostic.
claims.evidence: PRIME best Avg for all 6 base models on CMV, e.g. 34.13 vs 32.24 DUAL on Llama-3.1-8B (Table 3).
R1-distilled models below non-personalized base on CMV for Llama-8B (25.18 vs 26.58) and Qwen-7B (23.36 vs 27.89) (Table A3).

claims.claim: PRIME uses the specific user's history rather than popularity.
claims.evidence: Swapping in another user's LoRA and profile lowers scores, most for the most similar users (Fig. 2, App. D).

limits: Two benchmarks cannot cover the range of personalization tasks, e.g. long-form personalization.
Models only up to 14B parameters, for budget reasons.
Inference is costly: 10-20 hours per model on one A40 or L40 GPU.
reading: Combining both memories is not consistently better: DUAL is below SM alone for Qwen2.5-7B (28.71 vs 30.20) and Llama-3.2-3B (28.87 vs 30.25), which is why the final PRIME drops episodic memory (§6, §7.1).

On LaMP, PRIME is below DUAL on LaMP-3 (MAE .223 vs .188) and LaMP-5 (ROUGE-1 47.3 vs 52.2), and all non-OPPU methods trail OPPU, which trains on other users' data and uses Llama-2-7B, so that comparison differs in both data and base model.

The CMV test set was filtered to queries the base Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B get wrong without history (Hit@1 ≤ 0.3, Hit@3 ≤ 0.5), which removes 194 queries and lowers the non-personalized baseline for those two models by construction.
Every trained variant fits one adapter per user on the same task format it is tested on (task-oriented FT), so SM is closer to per-user supervised training than to a memory read at test time.
The main text reports Hit@3 and Avg; Table A3 shows Ministral-8B PRIME's Hit@3 (40.75) slightly below SM and DUAL (40.83).
